3. The case of the plaintiffs, inter alia, is that including other land, the alleged 0.21 acre of land belonged to Nabin Chandra Saha in khas and the rest of the land belonged to Gobinda Chandra Saha and Guruchandra Saha and in settlement survey Maliki Khatian No. 86 was published in the name of  Nabinchandra and Khatian No. 88 in the name of Gobinda Chandra and others; that in the said Khatian, one Ragunath Chandra was shown as permissive possessor in the remark column and after the survey the said Ragunath Chandra left for elsewhere, delivering the possession of the suit land in favour of Nab in Chandra Saha and others and by  an amicable settlement Nabin Chandra Saha got the entire land of suit plot with other land in his saham and other co-sharers got other land, that while possessing in such way Nabin Chandra died, leaving his only son, Jagabandhu  Saha, who inherited the same and as per provisions of State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, the khas Khamar title was converted into Raiyati jote title under the Government; that Jagabandu used to possess the suit land by erecting dwelling house which was a simple thatched hut but the remaining portion of land was an unused plot of land, 

 4. It is further stated that the defendant Nos. 1 to 5 namely, Rabindra Chandra Saha and Gopinath Saha, son of Jagabandhu Saha, Prodip Kumar Saha, Netai Chandra Saha and Narayan Chandra Saha, son of Anil Chandra Saha, proposed to Jagabandu Saha to rent the same on monthly basis for running the business of a carpenter by constructing a structure on about 2 decimals of land; that Jagabandu accepted the proposal and permitted them to use the land and to do their business as monthly tenant but after some period they became defaulters for a few months rent and about 4 years before the liberation war, they handed over the possession of the hut in lieu of the arrear rent in favour of Jagabandu Saha and went away elsewhere. It is further contended that subsequently the husband of the defendant No. 1 namely, Khondaker Golam Ahmed served in the police department and on transfer he came to Bajitpur and took the house from Jagabandu as a monthly tenant and in the meantime the War of Liberation started and Jagabandu Saha was killed, leaving 3 sons i.e the plaintiff Nos. 1 and 2 and Anil Chandra Saha, the predecessor of the plaintiff Nos. 3 to 5, who inherited the property and used to possess the suit land, keeping the husband of the defendant No.1, Ayesha Khatun, as a monthly tenant of the house on 02 decimal; that while possessing the land in this way, the husband of the defendant No. 1 Ayesha Khatun, died, leaving his widow and her son, Babul Khondaker, who remained as tenant; that husband of the defendant No.1 at his own cost re-constructed the old cracked house on the land of schedule No.2 and used to possess therein and that in the meantime Anil Chandra Saha died, leaving 3 sons, the plaintiff Nos. 3 to 5, who inherited their father's share of the property. It is also contended that due to a reckless movement and association with antisocial activities of the son of defendant No.1, she left the house and started living with her daughter permanently and thus the plaintiffs took possession of the aforesaid land; that with a view to grabbing the suit land, the defendant No.1 filed a suit being No. 86 of 1990 in the Court of Senior Assistant Judge, Bajitpur,and through conversation with other villagers, the plaintiffs came to know about the other suit No. 86 of 1990 in which the plaintiffs impleaded themselves as defendants and contested the suit; that although Jogesh Chandra Sutradhar did not inherit the suit land, beyond the knowledge of Jogesh, the defendant No.1 created a forged deed dated 15-5-1969 by false personification showing Jogesh Chandra Sutradhar as vendor in favour of the defendant No.1, Ayesha Khatun, as purchaser which the plaintiffs for the first time came to know from the plaint of the suit filed by the defendant No.1 and on 8-1-1998 the plaintiffs obtained the certified copy of the RoR record and became aware of the fact that in absence of Jagabandu Saha, the tenant, Jogesh Chandra Sutradhar and others collusively and illegally entered their names in RoR and kept this in secret; that the said record was wrongly prepared in the names of an interestless person and no portion of the suit land is enlisted as enemy property; that the husband of the defendant No.1 also obtained a false lease in VP case No. 31 of 1978-79 narrating that the suit land was enlisted as enemy property which also created no right and title; that long after the filing of Other Suit No. 86 of 1990, the defendant No.1 Ayesha Khatun with a view to establishing her illegal claim firmly, constructed a thatched hut on the land of schedule No.2 land and dispossessed the plaintiffs forcibly. In these circumstances, the plaintiffs were constrained to file the suit. 

 5. The defendant No.1, Ayesha Khatun, who is now dead, contested the suit by filing a written statement, denying the material allegations of the plaint. 

 6. The case of' the defendant No. 1 Ayesha, inter alia, is that out of the entire land, a portion of suit land measuring 0.21 acre was recorded in the name of Nab in Chandra Saha in CS khatian No. 86 and the rest of the land in the name of Gobinda Chandra Saha and others in Khatian No. 88; that Gogan Chandra Sutradhar, the father of the defendant Nos.2 to 5, took pattan of the unused suit land and lived there by erecting a dwelling house and subsequently he died, leaving 4 sons namely, Jogesh Chandra, Mohonabashi, Mohananda and Nirananda and with the enactment of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, they became tenants of the Government and while possessing the same adversely, the SA record was correctly prepared and finally published in the names of the defendant Nos. 2 to 5; that while the defendant Nos. 2 to 5 were possessing the entire land by an amicable settlement, Jogesh Chandra Sutradhar got the suit land in his saham and by registered deed No. 2373 dated 15-5-1969 transferred the same in favour of this defendant No.1, Ayesha Khatun who since 1969 had been living thereon by erecting a dwelling house and paying rent to the government; that thereafter, since the land is situated within Bajitpur Municipality, the defendant No.1, Ayesha Khatun, opened a holding in her name and paid the municipal taxes and present record was also prepared in her name. It is further contended that while she came to know about the enlistment of 75% of the land as enemy property, she filed Other Suit No. 86 of 1996 in the Court of the Senior Assistant Judge, Bajitpur in which the plaintiffs were subsequently added as defendants and her husband was also buried in the same suit land. It is further contended that the defendant No.1, Ayesha Khatun, became astonished to know the claim of the present plaintiffs that Jogesh Chandra by an amicable settlement got the suit land 60 years ago and the plaintiffs got the suit land by inheritance, and that taking the advantage of the helpless condition of the defendant No.1, Ayesha Khatun, the plaintiffs brought this suit on false grounds which is liable to be dismissed. 

 28. The contesting defendant No.1 admitted in his written statement that the suit land originally belonged to Nobin Chandra Saha who died, leaving the only son, Gogobondu Saha, who inherited the suit land. DW 1, Panna Begum, also admitted in her deposition that Nabin Chandra Saha was the original owner and the plaintiffs are his subsequent heirs. The plaintiffs have also submitted the CS Khatian No.86 of Nabin Chandra Saha Exhibit-1. The plaintiffs have also adduced corroborative and reliable evidence in this respect. So, it is evident from the above discussion that the suit land including 'Kha' scheduled land belonged to Nobin Chandra Saha, the predecessor of the plaintiffs and the plaintiffs inherited the same by inheritance. 

 33. In the written statement, it is simply stated that Gogan Chandra Sutradhar took lease from superior landlord but it is not stated how, when and from whom the said lease was taken. All these are the material facts which ought to have been written in the written statement. As regards that object of pleadings, in the case of Ganesh Trading Co vs Moji Ram reported AIR 1978 SC 484, the Supreme Court has observed; 

 "2. Every pleading shall contain, and contain only a statement in a concise form of the material facts on which the party pleading relies for his claim or defence as the case may be ..... " 

 36. In this instant case, the particular of lease of Gogan Chandra Sutradhar from the superior landlord is a material fact which ought to have been stated specifically. The contesting defendant alleges that her predecessor got the 'Kha' scheduled land by way of lease and the contesting defendant in order to succeed is to prove such assertion both by documentary andoral evidences. But the contesting defendant No-1, Ayesha Khatun, neither disclosed the particulars of the lease nor did she prove it by documentary or oral evidence. The contesting defendant did not file any document of the lease. The contesting. defendant filed two zamidari Dakhalies marked Exhibit 'Kha' and 'Kha' (1) wherein the names of the tenants were written as Mohandrao Sutradhar and Jogesh Chandra Sutradhar whereas in the written statement, it was shown that Gogan, the father of defendant Nos.2 to 5, took the lease from superior landlord. These material discrepancies clearly indicate the falsity of the lease.
